clue.text: Sort of lily to cultivate in religious community

indicators.note: the cultivating word is placed inside the community word, as the clue says

parts.note: a friary is a community of friars
to till is to cultivate the soil

explanation.surface: A gardener plans to grow a particular lily within the grounds of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: The fritillary is a bulbous plant of the lily family, with chequered bell-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Baby's toy rabbit

explanation.surface: A child's plaything is a bunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is not the animal but British slang for talking on and on, as in 'rabbit on', which is what you do when you rattle on.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattle is a noisy toy shaken by infants; to rattle on and to rabbit on both mean to chatter at length.

clue.text: Excessively bad driver finally disqualified, taking blame

indicators.note: the driver's final letter is disqualified, so it is struck off the end

parts.note: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is literature's famously reckless motorist
fault means blame or responsibility

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist banned at last is held responsible for the crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad driver' is Mr Toad, the car-mad hero of Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows; losing his last letter leaves TOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to a fault means doing it to an extreme degree, even to excess.

clue.text: It's admissible to run away before I get married

parts.note: leg it is informal British for run away
to mate is to pair up, as animals do

explanation.surface: Someone argues that it is acceptable to elope before marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate is allowed or valid under the rules, so it can be accepted.

clue.text: Well-informed about king — a brutal person

indicators.note: the phrase for the brute goes about the king, enclosing him

parts.note: a beast is a brutal, savage person
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A clever monarch turns out to be a savage tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep abreast of events is to stay up to date and knowledgeable about them.

clue.text: Over record, the old cry

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: An old-timer complains loudly over a vintage vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a short sharp cry, as of a dog in pain.

clue.text: Make out with quiet woman after start of month

indicators.note: the quiet woman comes after the month's opening day in the answer

parts.note: the first of December is written DEC I
p is the musical marking piano, soft
her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with a shy lady at the beginning of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' looks like a smooch; it means to read or understand. 'Start of month' is not M but the first day of December.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher a message is to work out or read what it says.

clue.text: Calmness of temper making boy love girl

parts.note: Phil is a boy's name
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
Sophy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lad's affection for a lass gives him a serene outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking things philosophically means bearing them with equanimity and composure.

clue.text: Men she managed to get in a tangle

indicators.note: the letters are managed, handled and arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Men she handled managed to get themselves into a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to catch or entangle, as in a net.

clue.text: Someone unfamiliar seen by park-keeper beside road

indicators.note: the keeper's word is set beside the road's abbreviation

parts.note: ST is short for street, a road
a ranger looks after a park or forest

explanation.surface: A park warden spots a newcomer by the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is a person one does not know.

clue.text: Slip around slippery surface, turning right round — that's exceptional

indicators.note: the whole combination turns right round, read from end to start
the slip goes around the slippery surface, enclosing it

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or small error
ice is a slippery surface

explanation.surface: A skater slips on the ice and does a full spin, which is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning right round' applies to the whole container, so the slip with the ice inside is read backwards as one run; 'slippery surface' is a definition-like phrase, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal word for special or outstanding.

clue.text: Options people accepted

parts.note: men are people
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Choices are open to the people who were let in.
explanation.walkthrough: U, from 'U and non-U', labels upper-class or socially acceptable usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of choices, in a restaurant or on a computer.

clue.text: Ceremonial official became rare after reorganisation

annotationWithheld.why: Ceremonial official became rare after reorganisation (4,6): the anagram of BECAME RARE gives MACEBEARER, but the held answer is MACEBBAAEE, three letters off, beyond what answerTypo accepts
annotationWithheld.clue: Ceremonial official became rare after reorganisation

clue.text: After an operation you may be laughing

definitions.text: After an operation you may be laughing

parts.words: After an operation you may be laughing
parts.note: a surgical patient has sutures in the wound, and a phrase for that also means helpless with laughter

explanation.surface: A post-surgery patient may find themselves laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in stitches means laughing uncontrollably, and literally having sutures in a wound.

clue.text: Liberated, I learnt not to be bigoted

indicators.note: the letters are liberated from their order and freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Once freed from prejudice, I learned not to be narrow-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: An intolerant person refuses to accept views or people different from their own.

clue.text: Former PM seen to talk and act in exaggerated fashion

parts.note: chat is talk
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: An ex-premier is seen chattering and overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: William Pitt the Elder, British Prime Minister 1766-68, was the Earl of Chatham.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitt the Elder, made Earl of Chatham, led the British government in the 1760s.

clue.text: A strange, white calla

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
lily, as in lily-white, means pure white

explanation.surface: An odd pale calla is noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The calla is another name for the arum lily, a plant with a white trumpet-shaped spathe.

clue.text: Bit of tack — sound pleased it's returned

indicators.note: the two pieces together are returned, read backwards from end to start

parts.note: a contented cat purrs
the word is used as its letters

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies with pleasure when a lost piece of riding gear comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the whole of PURRITS round to give STIRRUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is a horse's riding gear, of which a stirrup, the rider's footrest, is one part.

clue.text: Got up to make a delivery — it features something from florist

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
in cricket the bowler delivers the ball, so to bowl is to make a delivery

explanation.surface: A courier rose early to deliver an order from the flower shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a delivery' suggests a courier; in cricket a bowler's ball is called a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a dish for displaying cut flowers, especially roses bought from a florist.

clue.text: Mismanage contract

explanation.surface: Botching a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up is to bungle something, or to tighten and wrinkle, as one does one's eyes or face.

clue.text: Censor showing endless ebullience breezing round page

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the page's abbreviation
breezing suggests letters blown about and scattered
the word loses its last letter, leaving it endless

explanation.surface: A censor shows tireless high spirits while breezing through the manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final E of 'ebullience'; 'breezing' rearranges what is left into BLUEENCIL, and 'round' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil a text is to cut or censor it, from the editor's coloured pencil.

clue.text: Form of transport reportedly available to butcher

indicators.note: reportedly means the transport word is as spoken, a matter of how it sounds

parts.note: a sleigh is a sledge, a form of snow transport

explanation.surface: A vehicle is said to be at a meat-seller's disposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to kill them brutally, to massacre.

clue.text: Islands since found to contain unknown mineral source

indicators.note: the word for since is found to contain the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: as can mean since, because
z is a mathematical unknown
ore is rock from which a mineral is extracted

explanation.surface: Explorers discover that a group of islands holds deposits of an unidentified mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azores are an Atlantic archipelago belonging to Portugal.

clue.text: Daughter abandons flirtation for marriage

indicators.note: the daughter abandons the word, so her letter is dropped

parts.note: dalliance is casual flirtation

explanation.surface: A girl gives up a fling in favour of a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union, and a marriage is the classic union between families.

clue.text: Something fishy up? Here's member of drug squad

indicators.note: in a down answer the word goes up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herrings, 37.5 gallons

explanation.surface: Something suspicious is going on, and a drug squad officer is here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' seems to mean suspicious; it is a cran, a measure of herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics agent.

clue.text: Armaments can crush any power

indicators.note: crush means the letters are crushed together and squeezed into a new order

explanation.surface: Weapons are able to overwhelm any nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry is weapons collectively, the arms of a force.

clue.text: Cake presented by girl, end first

indicators.note: the name's last letter moves to the front, so its end comes first

parts.note: Claire is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl brings out a cake, end first.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and iced.

clue.text: Almost provide finishing touch — it's unusual for a rich man

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: to cap it all is to provide a finishing touch

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: the word is used as its letters

explanation.surface: Putting the final flourish on something is unusual for a wealthy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last L of CAP IT ALL; 'unusual' rearranges ITS into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalist is a wealthy person who invests money in business.
